by: google/gemini-3.8-flash (machine translation of the OCR text, 20-Nov-2026; not checked)
segments: this one sent to the wife of Joscelin and his son,
that they should instruct Gregory, the Catholicos of the Armenians who was in the monastery of the Lake,
to come and dwell with him,
and to be a helper to him.
When he came,
he acted deceitfully against Michael,
and took all his possessions and drove him out;
and he himself remained in Qal'ah Rumaytā.
And in that same year,
which is the year one thousand four hundred and sixty-one {1461, OCR: 1444?},
(544 of the Arabs?):
Sayf al-Dīn, son of Zangī, the lord of Mosul, took the city of Dārā from Timurtash, the lord of Mardin;
and he went and encamped against Mardin as well.
Then Timurtash, when he was bested by him,
gave him his daughter as a wife,
and made peace with him.
And when Sayf al-Dīn returned to Mosul,
he fell ill and died.
And in his place arose Qutb al-Dīn Mawdūd, his brother;
and he took his wife, the daughter of Timurtash.
Then certain of the nobles sent to Nūr al-Dīn in Aleppo,
and asked that he should come to them.
And immediately, without delay, with seventy horsemen, Nūr al-Dīn arrived at Sinjār,
and they surrendered it to him.
And he sent to Qara Arslan, the lord of the Fortress [Ḥiṣn Kayfā],
and promised him the Fortress of Haytham, that he might come to his aid.
And Qutb al-Dīn, his brother, gathered an army,
and went out to Tell A'far to meet Nūr al-Dīn.
Then the nobles arose [and intervened between them],
and he gave Homs,
because it had belonged to Sayf al-Dīn,
to Nūr al-Dīn.
And Nūr al-Dīn returned Sinjār to Qutb al-Dīn,
and left and returned to Aleppo.
And in this year there was a flood in Ḥiṣn Ziyād on the 23rd of Ab,
and it swept away a youth and his mother, and two she-mules (and two mules) and a donkey,
and they were all drowned.
And in the year 1462
(1462 of the Greeks?):
the wife of the lord of Erzincan choked him with a bowstring,
and brought his brother from Divriği,
and he took her as a wife and reigned.
And a certain Turkish emir went up to the Greek monastery of Sirika {OCR?} in Pontus,
and took the golden cross in which there was a portion of the wood of the crucifixion,
and which performed miracles in that region.
And after a large ransom which he took from the monks,
he returned it again to the monastery.
Then the Greeks, who had blasphemed against Saint Mar Barsawma, were ashamed and confounded, saying:
"If there were power in him,
why did he abandon [it] to Joscelin?"
